summary.text: In Mandarin, 的 marks possession or links a modifier to a noun. The current graph is visibly 白 + 勺; one analysis assigns 白 the meaning “white” and 勺 a sound role. The traditional account quoted for 旳(的) instead gives 日 + 勺 for “bright” and reports 的 as the common form. The date and process connecting these analyses are uncertain.

formation.text: One analysis treats current 的 as phonosemantic: 白 contributes the meaning “white,” and 勺 supplies a sound cue. In Zhengzhang Old Chinese, 勺 *pljewɢ and 的 *pleːwɢ are similar, supporting a plausible phonetic role without fixing the precise historical pronunciation. The traditional account quoted for 旳(的) instead assigns 日 + 勺 to “bright”; the graphic relationship remains uncertain.

components.text: In the traditional analysis of 旳, 日 is the semantic component for “bright.” This account does not establish when or how the graph came to be written with 白 in 的.
In 旳, 勺 is identified as the sound component. 勺 also means “ladle,” but that separate meaning does not make 旳 a spelling for “ladle.”

sound_limitation.text: The cited Zhengzhang comparison is between 勺 and 的, not the scoped host 旳, so it does not establish the historical sound relation in the 旳 analysis.

sound.text: In Modern Mandarin, 勺 is read sháo and 旳 dì. These current readings do not establish an ancient sound relationship.

components.text: In one analysis of 的, 白 contributes the category “white.” Its graphic relationship to 日 in the traditional analysis of 旳 is unresolved.
In one analysis of 的, 勺 supplies a sound cue. Zhengzhang reconstructs 勺 as *pljewɢ and 的 as *pleːwɢ; their similarity supports a plausible role but does not settle the precise historical relation.

sound.text: In Zhengzhang Old Chinese, one reading of 勺 is reconstructed as *pljewɢ and 的 as *pleːwɢ. Their similarity supports a plausible sound relationship; reconstructions from different systems should not be combined.
In Modern Mandarin, 勺 is read sháo and 的 de. This current comparison does not establish their historical sound relation.

history.text: The received Shuo Gua text uses 的顙 in a description of a horse. A traditional explanation links the phrase with 旳, meaning “bright,” or with the brightness of white; a modern dictionary glosses the phrase as a white forehead. These readings do not date the graph or settle the phrase’s interpretation. A 2012 dictionary prints 旳(的) as a combined headword with dī and dí reading lines; those are readings in that edition, not an ancient reconstruction or a general current reading for 旳.

The traditional account calls 的 the common form of 旳. The selected image shows 旳 as represented in the Shuowen seal-script tradition; it is a modern drawing, not an ancient inscription. The date and process of the graphic change are uncertain.
的 is also recorded with the meaning “target.” This may extend from a brightness-related or white-mark sense, or may belong to a separate root; the relationship and chronology remain unsettled.

The possessive and attributive particle was written 底 before 的 replaced that spelling. One account dates the substitution to a 1238 stele, while a secondary survey reports 底 in use from Wei–Jin through Song. This spelling change does not show that the particle’s meaning developed from “bright.”

uncertainties.text: The traditional analysis of 旳 uses 日, while a separate analysis of 的 uses 白. The date and process connecting these forms, including any continuous graphic sequence, remain uncertain.
The relationship, if any, among brightness, the white-forehead expression, and target uses is unsettled; no semantic path or chronology among them is established.
The particle’s spoken origin is disputed. Proposals connect 底 with 之, 者, or the demonstrative 底; the accounts do not settle among them.

senses.text: Dictionary sources record 的 with the meanings ‘mark in a target’ and ‘target.’ A traditional commentary proposes that the target sense extended from the brightness associated with 旳, while another account allows an independent root; the relationship and chronology remain unsettled. The Han gloss ‘bright’ belongs specifically to 旳 and is not established here as a sense of 的.

senses.period: Late Middle Chinese onward; precise chronology disputed
senses.text: In Mandarin, de marks possession or links a modifier to a noun. Historical accounts report 底 as an earlier spelling before 的 replaced it; the spoken word’s origin remains disputed.

limitations.text: The traditional ‘bright’ gloss belongs to 旳. The received 的顙 phrase is interpreted as a white forehead, but does not establish that 的 itself had this sense or date it.

The traditional commentary proposes a connection between the brightness associated with 旳 and the target sense of 的. The evidence does not establish that semantic development or its chronology; an independent target root remains possible.
The proposed grammatical origins of the particle remain disputed; the evidence does not establish a single development from 之, 者, or demonstrative 底.
The traditional account reports 的 as a common form of 旳, but the transition’s date and process are uncertain.

items.caption: In the Shuowen seal-script tradition, 旳 places 日 beside 勺. Its traditional analysis assigns 日 the meaning “bright” and 勺 a sound role; the account calls 的 a common form but does not date or explain the change.
items.alt: A closed, rounded 日 shape with an interior horizontal line sits beside a separate 勺 form, whose flowing line bends back and has a short horizontal mark inside.
items.selection_reason: This readable rendering shows the traditional side-by-side 日 + 勺 analysis, contrasting with current 的, visibly 白 + 勺. The relationship between the forms remains unresolved.
